A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OT Score work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, confidence-score benchmark results, digit-noise tests, and SDOT-DA evaluations in Section 6 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 reports confidence-score experiments, OT-weighted adaptation results, and model-comparison analyses in Section 5, alongside synthetic experiments in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The core score computation is retained; Algorithm 1 merely specifies class-mean inputs already used in v1. However, v2 adds CoWA-JMDS training weights of 2 × OT score × JMDS, computing OT scores from pre-adaptation features, and removes the standalone SDOT-DA labeling algorithm from v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: v2 removes Office-31 evaluation and the binary MNIST/USPS scenarios with Gaussian corruption. It adds label-free model comparison, including the pixel-inverted FLIP-USPS source scenario. Office-Home, ImageCLEF-DA, VisDA-2017, and the synthetic cluster scenarios remain represented.

E2.justification: New SFUDA accuracy comparisons include CoWA, BAIT, SHOT, NRC, ELR, CPD, SFIT, and AdaCon in Tables 2–3. The earlier standalone SDOT-DA comparisons, including GtA, ADDA, SRADA, RevGrad, DRCN, and ETD, disappear. Maxprob, Ent, Cossim, and JMDS remain the AURC comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes source training from 100 epochs to 50 for Office-Home/ImageCLEF-DA and 10 for VisDA. VisDA GMM evaluation switches from ResNet-50 to ResNet-101, digits from VGG16 to ResNet-18, and OT regularization from 0.5 to 0.0001. New adaptation-accuracy and model-comparison protocols are introduced. These reported revisions do not establish that retained DSAN results were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's clean/noisy binary-digit tests, difficult digit-pair analyses, and fixed 10% confidence-filtering results are removed. v2 adds mean-score versus accuracy analysis and the inverted-source comparison in Figure 2 and Table 4. The overlapping-cluster and class-imbalance analyses are retained and relocated, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 provides no seed counts or variability estimates. v2 introduces mean ± standard deviation over three independent seeds for the added reweighting experiments in Tables 6–7. This reporting remains limited to those experiments; the AURC comparisons retain point estimates.

E6.justification: GMM AURC results are replaced under revised settings: for example, OT Score averages change from 0.1735 to 0.1628 on Office-Home and from 0.2916 to 0.1704 on VisDA. The full DSAN table's numerical entries are unchanged. New reweighting results report 73.0 versus CoWA's 72.5 on Office-Home and 87.8 versus 86.9 on VisDA. Earlier digit and Office-31 result entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 8, restated as Theorem 10 in Appendix C, claiming a classification-error bound conditional on confidence filtering under sub-Gaussian concentration and singleton source representatives. It includes a new boundary-distance derivation. The earlier label-preservation results and class-imbalance theorem are retained, with renumbering and relocation.

C1.justification: The title and abstract explicitly foreground source-free UDA. The introduction and contributions add claims that OT-based training reweighting improves adaptation and that mean OT score enables label-free model selection. v1 emphasized post-hoc confidence assessment and filtering, with training-time use discussed as future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that pre-adaptation features reduce pseudo-label confirmation bias and interprets mean OT score as an ordinal performance proxy. Its conclusion newly acknowledges biased class-proportion estimates from unreliable pseudo-labels, replacing v1's emphasis on retaining more source information. The synthetic class-imbalance applicability caveat remains.

D1.justification: The implementation recipe updates backbones, training durations, and regularization, and adds the feature source, score normalization, and scaling factor for CoWA integration. The RTX 4070 hardware disclosure and detailed DSAN optimizer/scheduler settings are retained. Neither PDF supplies a code-access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion and citations on conditional alignment, OT entanglement, and confidence-based SFUDA, including Koç et al., Karim et al., and Litrico et al., plus references for the new comparators. The earlier positioning around OT geometry versus cluster-based confidence and the existing theoretical background remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivation, and conclusion are substantially revised. Related work moves from the main text to Appendix A, synthetic experiments move into Appendix D, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around AURC comparison, training reweighting, and model comparison. The standalone SDOT-DA appendix is removed.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates the earlier duplicated AURC displays, removes the binary-digit and SDOT-DA tables, and adds adaptation-accuracy, source-comparison, and variability tables plus a score–accuracy plot. Existing synthetic figures are relocated and renumbered. Typography, headings, and figure/table placement also change throughout the document.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful controlled reweighting comparisons, model-comparison evidence, and three-seed variability. However, it removes v1's noise-robustness tests while retaining broad confidence claims. The new Theorem 8/10 proof also stops at a class-cell probability without establishing the stated error bound conditional on confidence filtering. These practical gains and unresolved theoretical and evidential tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
